title: OPK Package
description: Schema for package.json, the manifest of a shareable unit of OES content in the Open Package Format (OPK), version 0.1.0.

$schema.description: Optional. Points an editor (e.g. VS Code) at this document's JSON Schema for inline validation/autocomplete. A JSON-tooling convention, not part of the OES content model — an OES parser ignores it like any other unrecognized field.

opk_version.description: Any 0.1.x patch release of OPK — see the Versioning & Conformance policy for what's allowed to change in a patch.

name.description: {namespace}/{package}, both kebab-case. The namespace is what a registry grants ownership of; OPK takes no position on how.

version.description: SemVer for the package's content, independent of every spec version inside it. Major when an existing reference into this content would now mean something different.

description.description: One or two sentences, for a listing.

license.description: SPDX identifier. Strongly recommended on anything published — content with no stated license is content nobody can safely reuse.

language.description: BCP 47 tag for the content's primary language.

oes_version.description: The OES release this package was authored against. Lets a consumer check compatibility once rather than inspecting every document's own version field.

entry.description: The document a consumer opens first. Named explicitly so no consumer has to guess or probe for it.

path.description: Path relative to the package root, e.g. "course.json".

requires.description: What a consumer must implement to render this package.

profiles.description: Conformance profiles — see the Conformance profiles section. A consumer that doesn't implement them SHOULD refuse the package rather than render it partially.

dependencies.description: Other packages this one needs, as {name: semver range}. A release range, not a location — OPK takes no position on where packages live. Distinct from a course's `prerequisites`, which are pedagogical.

digest.description: SHA-256 over a canonical listing of every file path and its own SHA-256, sorted by path — independent of archive format, file ordering, and timestamps. Covers every file including prose and images, which per-document content_hash does not. Absent while authoring; a registry SHOULD require it on publish.

files.description: The manifest. Absent while authoring; a registry SHOULD require it on publish, since it is what makes `digest` reproducible and lets a consumer verify a partial fetch.

path.description: Relative to the package root. MUST NOT escape it.

source.description: Where this content was originally sourced or adapted from, if it wasn't authored directly for OES — e.g. produced by an importer against another platform's content. Entirely optional; omit for content authored directly. Distinct from this document's own top-level `license`, which describes this OES document's license, not what it was adapted from — the original may be more restrictive (or simply different) and belongs in `source.license` instead. Also distinct from `downloadable`/`local_path`: `source` records provenance, it never by itself grants redistribution rights to the underlying document file.

platform.description: Free-text label for the originating platform or site. Deliberately not an enum — OES doesn't hard-code or endorse any specific platform; any importer fills in whatever's accurate.

license.description: The ORIGINAL content's license or terms of use at the source. Free text, not constrained to SPDX like this document's own `license` field.

retrieved_at.description: When this content was fetched/adapted from the source.

note.description: Free-text context an importer or author wants to record.
